newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE euroyen end flat, 2-month CD yield rises.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE euroyen end flat, 2-month CD yield rises.

text.p: The key December three-month euroyen futures contract settled flat on Thursday, relinquishing early gains after comments by the Bank of Japan governor that it was important to act pre-emptively to achieve continued growth without inflation.
In the open market, about 205 billion yen worth of two-month certificates of deposit (CDs) were issued at 0.59 percent, the highest yield since August 21, 1996.
The rise in the two-month CD rate reflected market concerns about higher interest rates, traders said.

Although market players do not expect the BOJ to tighten credit immediately after the release of the key "tankan" survey on June 25, they feel that interest rates may rise in the following months, a trust bank trader said.
The large issuance probably was due to needs on the part of issuers to roll over maturing CDs, a city bank trader said.
One city bank issued 60 billion yen worth of the two-month CDs at 0.59 percent, while another issued 145 billion yen worth, the trader said.

Key December euroyen futures rose in early morning due to a rise in Japanese government bonds, but their early gains were pared when BOJ Governor Yasuo Matsushita said it was important to conduct pre-emptive policy steps in order to realise continued growth without inflation.
The comment rekindled concerns about the possibility of higher rates, although most market players do not think the BOJ will raise short-term interest rates very soon, traders said.
Traders said they expected the December to move in a range from 98.80 to 98.90 in the near term.
The December's day session turnover was 39,244 contracts.
The Bank of Japan drained a net 300 billion yen from the money market on Thursday morning against a projected fund surplus of 480 billion yen.
The weighted average of the key overnight call rate is likely to be 0.48 percent on Thursday, down from 0.50 percent on Wednesday, traders said.

Large-scale tax payments from the private sector had led to increased fund demand and firmness in the overnight call rate over the last several days. The lack of such payments on Thursday caused the key overnight call rate to decline, a city bank trader said.
There was very little movement in the interest rate swap market (IRS), trader for a foreign brokerage house said.
Three-year IRS rates were quoted at 1.74/78 percent, up from 1.72/76 percent on Wednesday.
The 10-year IRS rates were quoted at 2.95/99 percent, up from 2.94/98 percent on Wednesday.
